Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 100, verse 1:

(p-671) Surah "Al-'Adiyat" (The Chargers)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the snorting chargers,﴾ He swears by the horses of the warriors that run and then snort. "Al-Dabh" (snorting) is the sound of their breaths when they run. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he imitated it, saying: "Ah, ah." The accusative of "dabhan" is governed by an implied verb: "yadbahna dabhan" (they snort a snorting).

Al-Nasafi, *Madarik al-Tanzil* (commentary on Surah 100, verse 2):

﴿By those that strike sparks﴾: they kindle the fire of al-Hubahib (a proverbial fire), which is what flies off from their hooves.

﴿Striking sparks﴾: they strike the stones with their hooves, striking them. *Al-qadh* (striking) means *al-sakk* (striking hard), and *al-iraʾ* (kindling) means bringing out fire. One says: "He struck and kindled" (*qadaha fa-awra*), and "He struck and got nothing" (*qadaha fa-asmada*).

*Qadhan* (striking) is in the accusative by the same governing element that puts *ḍabhan* (panting) in the accusative.

﴿Fal-mughirat﴾ (by the ones who charge), who attack the enemy.

﴿Subhan﴾ (at dawn), at the time of the morning.
﴿So they raise up thereby a cloud of dust﴾, meaning: thereby, at that time, they stir up dust.

Surah 100, verse 5: Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil)

﴿Then they burst into the midst thereby﴾, at that time,

﴿a throng﴾, from the throngs of the enemy. And "wasatahu" means "tawassatahu" (penetrated it, got into the middle of it). It was said: the pronoun refers to the place of the raid, or to the enemy, which is indicated by "wal-'adiyat" (by the chargers).

And he coordinated "fa-'atharna" (and raised dust) with the verb whose place the active participle has taken, because the meaning is: "and those which ran, then struck sparks, then made raids, then raised dust." And the response of the oath:
Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord﴾, meaning he is ungrateful (kafur); that is, indeed he is, regarding his Lord's blessings, especially so, exceedingly ungrateful.

﴿And indeed he﴾, meaning and indeed the human being,

﴿is, to that﴾, meaning, to his ingratitude (كُنُودِهِ, *kunūdihi*),

﴿a witness﴾, meaning he testifies against himself. Or it means: and indeed God is a witness to his ingratitude, in the manner of a warning (*al-wa'īd*).

Qur'an 100:8: ﴿And indeed, in his love of wealth, he is severe.﴾ And indeed, because of his love of wealth, he is stingy and tight-fisted; or: indeed, in his love of wealth he is strong, while in his love of the worship of Allah he is weak.

﴿Does he not know﴾, the human being,

﴿when what is in the graves is overturned﴾, is raised up,

﴿what is in the graves﴾, of the dead. And "mā" here has the meaning of "man" (who).
{And what is in the breasts is made apparent}, meaning: what is in them of good and evil is separated out.

Surah 100, verse 11: "Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully Aware of them."

﴿Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully Aware of them﴾: [meaning] He is Knowing, so He will recompense them for their deeds, whether good or evil. "That Day" is singled out for mention, although He knows them at all times, because the recompense takes place on that Day.
